title: Call Routing Gateway and Semantic Name Resolution for Legacy Functions
creator: Rohan Patel
description:
Summary: Build a lightweight call-routing gateway that accepts OpenAI-style tool calls from hosted API clients and routes them to Redwood legacy function handlers. The gateway implements semantic name resolution, fuzzy alias matching, argument-schema translation, streaming passthrough for partial outputs, and graceful fallbacks to prevent customer-visible failures.

Background: Customers and existing SDKs use a mix of OpenAI 'tools' and our legacy 'functions' shapes. Naming mismatches, parameter schema differences, and streaming behavior cause integration friction and production incidents (see incidents linked below). Current shims are ad-hoc and duplicated across runtime components. We need a consolidated, low-latency compatibility layer that is maintainable and observable.

Goals:
- Route OpenAI-style tool call payloads to the correct legacy function handler with >99.9% accuracy for common mappings.
- Preserve streaming semantics: allow function outputs to stream tokens back to the original client when the underlying handler supports chunked responses.
- Provide a registry of canonical names + aliases and a deterministic resolution algorithm (exact match, alias lookup, semantic similarity fallback) with audit logs.
- Translate argument/response schemas (JSON coercion, required/optional mapping) and report translation warnings to logs and the Console.
- Fail fast with a standardized error envelope and automatic fallback policies (e.g., call compatible variant, return structured error to LLM for retry).

Design notes and trade-offs:
- We propose an in-process gateway that lives on the serving runtime path as an opt-in route for customers flagged for compatibility. This minimizes network hops but increases runtime surface. Alternative was a sidecar service (easier to iterate), but benchmarks show ~6-8ms extra RTT for a sidecar under load; we prefer in-process for P1 latency targets.
- Name resolution: primary store is the Canonical Tool Registry (dependency ENG-51830). For ambiguous names we use alias table + a lightweight vector-semantic fallback using title+description embeddings restricted to top-5 candidates to avoid surprises. Trade-off: vector fallback adds infra and cold-start cost but improves developer UX for misnamed tools.
- Schema translation: implement a small rule engine (coercions, defaults, deprecated param mapping). We intentionally avoid heavy runtime JSON schema validation for performance reasons; validation runs asynchronously in parallel when possible and emits warnings.
- Streaming: when the underlying function supports chunked responses, gateway must proxy partial outputs while also attaching structured metadata frames (start/end/trace ids). This requires small protocol additions to current streaming wire format and Console parsers.

Implementation plan:
1) Spike (completed): prototype name-resolution library + vector fallback (benchmarks included in links).
2) Registry integration (in-progress): read-only cache and subscription to updates from ENG-51830.
3) Gateway implementation: routing rules, schema translation, streaming pass-through, error envelope.
4) Tests and QA: end-to-end tests with OpenAI-style tool payloads, chaos tests for partial streaming failures, compatibility matrices.
5) Rollout: feature-flagged rollout to internal customers -> beta customers -> default.

Metrics and success criteria:
- Mapping accuracy >= 99.9% for top-100 most-called tools during beta.
- Added latency <= 5ms p50 and <= 12ms p95 compared to baseline for routed calls.
- No increase in token-level error rate; reduce customer integration incidents by 75% for tool-calling flows.

Monitoring and observability: Emit resolution path traces, chosen-match confidence, translation warnings, fallback triggers, and streaming chunk metrics. Surface these in Console as a per-route breakdown and as alerts when fallback rate > 1%.

Rollback and mitigation: Feature flag controllable per-customer. If fallback rates or latency thresholds breach, flip flag to route calls to current stable shim.

Security: Because tool calls can trigger downstream side effects, this feature requires security review for injection, authorization, and auditability. KMS/cred usage for sensitive downstream calls must be enforced.

Artifacts and further reading: See linked design doc and prototype results for spike findings and benchmarks.

acceptance_criteria: Canonical registry integration: gateway uses ENG-51830 registry and logs when no mapping found.
Name resolution algorithm: exact -> alias -> semantic fallback; configurable thresholds.
Streaming passthrough: downstream chunked responses are forwarded with metadata frames and validated by unit tests.
Schema translation: common coercions implemented and translation warnings surface to Console.
Performance: added latency within targets and load-tested at 2x expected production QPS.
Security review completed and approval recorded before public rollout.
